newsitem.title: USA: Disney Q1 theme park revenues up 16 pct.
newsitem.headline: Disney Q1 theme park revenues up 16 pct.

text.p: Walt Disney Co said first quarter revenue at its theme parks and resorts division rose 16 percent to $1.2 billion and operating income rose 21 percent to $238 million.

Broadcasting revenues for the quarter increased four percent to $1.9 billion and operating income, excluding the gain on the sale of Los Angeles television station KCAL, increased 38 percent to $470 million.
Creative content revenues for the quarter increased five percent to $3.2 billion and operating income increased 10 percent to $719 million, Disney said.
The theme parks and resorts results for the quarter reflected record attendance levels and increased occupied room nights at Walt Disney World, Disney said.
Attendance gains were driven primarily by increased domestic tourist visitation at Walt Disney World, primarily due to the 25th Anniversary celebration, the company said.
Increased occupied room nights reflected higher occupancy as well as increased available rooms from Disney's BoardWalk Resort, which opened during the fourth quarter of the prior year, Disney said.
Results at Walt Disney World also reflected the successful opening of the World of Disney store at the Disney Village Marketplace during the quarter.
In addition, guest spending increased at both Walt Disney World and Disneyland.

Creative content results for the quarter reflected the successful domestic box office performance of the film "101 Dalmatians," "Ransom," and "The English Patient," the international theatrical success of "The Hunchback of Notre Dame," and the worldwide home video release of "Toy Story," Disney said.

Results for the quarter also reflected increased worldwide consumer products licensing of character merchandise, including 101 Dalmatians, and strong domestic holiday sales at the Disney Stores as well as their continued expansion, Disney said.

These increases were achieved despite the difficult comparisons to the prior-year domestic theatrical success of "Toy Story" and the prior-year home video strength of "Cinderella" domestically and "The Lion King" internationally, Disney said.
Broadcasting results for the quarter benefited from significant reductions in program amortization and other costs attributable to the acquisition of ABC, which became effective in February.

That was partially offset by lower network ratings. Results for the quarter also reflected revenue growth at ESPN and increased political advertising revenues at the owned and operated television stations.
"I am extremely pleased with the strong operating performance of all our major business groups during the first quarter," Disney chief executive Michael D. Eisner said.
"Walt Disney World led the way in our theme park division and the impressive box office performance of our holiday movies and home video releases also contributed to the company's results," he said.
"Worldwide merchandise licensing and ESPN continue to show strong growth and were significant factors in the company's overall performance," he said.

Results for the prior-year quarter on an as-reported basis do not reflect the ABC acquisition. To enhance comparability, operating results for the quarter ended December 31, 1995 have been presented on a pro forma basis which assumes the acquisition of ABC occurred at the beginning of the period.
